english.title: Fail to disclose information relevant to application for an Energy Act 2008 licence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), failed to disclose information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), which you knew or ought to have known, to be relevant to an application for

(A)_[a licence under section 4]_
(B)_[the consent of the Secretary of State for the purposes of a requirement, namely **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT..), imposed by virtue of section 6(4)]_
(C)_[the consent of **(..SPECIFY PERSON FROM WHOM CONSENT REQUIRED..) for the purposes of a requirement, namely **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT..), imposed by virtue of section 6(4)]_

of the Energy Act 2008
english.legislation: Contrary to section 9(4) and (5) of the Energy Act 2008.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
failed to disclose info
knew / ought to know
was relevant to application for licence / consent

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: A fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
